statements.t: With the election now behind us, we currently expect full-year 2026 political advertising to finish between $630 million and $640 million, with a midpoint 28% ahead of our $497 million in 2024 and 23% ahead of our $515 million total 2022, respectively.
The expected political advertising crowd out was more than offset by the contribution from our acquisitions, resulting in core advertising revenue growth of 1% compared to the third quarter of 2025.
Underlying non-political demand was stronger than we anticipated in our late September revised guidance.

We currently expect to use our incremental political cash to reduce our outstanding debt by $175 million to $200 million during the fourth quarter of 2026, which will further reduce our interest expense going into 2027.

Based on our current forecasts for the fourth quarter ending December 31, 2026, we anticipate the following key financial results, as outlined below in approximate ranges and as compared to the quarter ended December 31, 2025, as well as certain currently anticipated full-year financial results.
Our guidance includes estimated results for all television stations that were fully acquired as of November 6, 2026, as well as the ASM and WHPM stations.

Such risks, trends and uncertainties, which in some instances are beyond our control, include: the inability to achieve estimates of future revenue, expenses, capital expenditures, and income tax payments, the inability to complete the pending acquisitions within the expected timeframes, or at all, including as a result of the failure to obtain necessary FCC or other regulatory approvals, and other future events.
Conference Call Information We will host a conference call to discuss our operating results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, on Friday, November 6, 2026.

We currently expect that our routine capital expenditures will be approximately $45 million for the remainder of 2026, which includes several significant station construction projects and capital expenditures at Assembly Atlanta.
For the remainder of 2026, we currently expect to make income tax payments of approximately $20 million.

As of December 31, 2025, we have an aggregate of approximately $258 million of various state operating loss carryforwards, of which we expect that approximately $162 million will not be utilized due to Section 382 limitations under the Internal Revenue Code and those that will expire prior to utilization.
During the remainder of 2026, we do not expect to contribute to this pension plan.
